flawed_step: The conclusion does not follow. Having no short directed cycles does not make a digraph acyclic, so it need not have a source. A directed cycle of length 5 is allowed.
counterexample: Take vertices {0,1,2,3,4} and arcs 0→1, 1→2, 2→3, 3→4, 4→0 (the directed 5-cycle C5). It has no loops. Its only directed cycle is the whole 5-cycle, so there is no directed cycle of length 1, 2 or 3 (no pair of opposite arcs and no directed triangle). But every vertex has in-degree exactly 1, so no vertex has in-degree 0.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. The directed 5-cycle is a loopless digraph on 5 vertices. Its only directed cycle has length 5, so it satisfies the hypothesis. Yet every vertex has in-degree 1, so it has no vertex of in-degree 0.
